evidence: review/calls/review/chain.json: accepted_call=null, max_corrections=1, two structural_invalid attempts
why_no_semantic_repair.explanation: The runner reads repair findings only from an accepted review object and enters the shared semantic-repair phase only when review status is complete and findings exist. Structural failure produces review=null, so unaccepted candidate findings do not trigger repair. The one structural-correction budget was consumed; the semantic-repair budget was never entered.

raw_findings_summary.explanation: The Task captures access through the main entry module and direct invocation of that entry. It omits the separately documented ability to import granular functions directly from the API modules.

The date-format requirement applies shorthand to every operation that accepts a range. The comparison takes two DateRange objects and accesses their endpoints directly before forwarding either to the report parser.
The save-enabled condition also scopes suppression of standalone saves in the Task wording. Each batch iteration supplies save:false independently of the batch's save option.

The only represented module-evaluation route continues from settings initialization and client-slot initialization into the index's invocation-path test. Direct API imports evaluate their runtime dependencies without entering that index test. Direct storage or settings imports also have a smaller evaluation boundary that does not initialize the client slots.
The exit status gates npm, but the successful cd's working-directory version has no producer-to-consumer connection to npm. The destination controls where the installation takes place.

These seven instructions group the client getter and property lookup as resources. Each source occurrence obtains a particular client, then a fresh property value, then invokes a method on that client. Realtime puts the property in its selector object, while metadata formats the property into the request name. The grouped operands leave these executable connections missing.

The CFG omits the comparison's endpoint messages before their respective awaits, the URL workflows' initial count messages before iteration, and the failure messages carrying the original URL before each catch append. Those deliveries have different operands and occur at different points from the protected attempt messages.

The initializer declares a zero-argument call followed by a read of env. Its processing omits the possible acquisition from the configured .env source and the call's possible update to process.env. The post-call read alone cannot account for the new binding provenance.

The CFG already supplies the acquired client to each SDK instruction. The processed calls keep the request argument but drop its relationship to that client. A fixed service location cannot distinguish calls using different handle versions, including cache hits retaining creation-time credentials.

The protected cases cite the per-URL log in their conditions but never deliver the attempt message. Their post-entry error alternatives collapse a failed SDK request and a successful acquisition followed by a local failure into delivery plus exception alone. The latter alternative can acquire a real response before the caught value arises.

The annotation uses the same storage read for existence and content or directory entries. It also writes {recursive:true} as the directory payload. The source calls different filesystem interfaces at the supplied paths, and recursive:true is a mkdirSync control.

The compiler observations for internal wrappers include options construction operands and child replies inside ordinary local TypeScript calls. The code establishes direct local call and return to the wrapper. It provides no model handoff at those positions. The separately documented agent-facing analysis can make a returned version model-visible.

The realizations omit source-backed restrictions for the empty bulk path and for constituent batch saves. The empty bulk lookup returns before client acquisition, report delivery or saving. The sequential indexing batch always suppresses constituent saves and reaches its own save only after normal exhaustion with saving enabled.

Several return receivers lack demands for their stated content. The realtime entries seed request selectors without preserving returned grouping and count values. The high-level aggregates often seed only the named outer shape. The inspection demands cover verdict and coverage but retain whole optional sections without separately grounding presence and the documented contents. Save payload propagation does not establish these return requirements.

The initial process.env version has only a broad possible-sensitivity label, although GA4_PRIVATE_KEY can already exist before config() and has a specific source-backed credential range. The matching post-initialization label does not describe that earlier version.
